title: When the Protocol Wakes
premise: Lior Nystrom has spent a decade as the sole caretaker of the Halvard Seed Vault, ferrying genetic stock along a courier route through systems that severed contact after the Silence Wars. When a distress signal arrives in Old Meridian—a language extinct for two centuries—Lior realizes the sender is a colony ship thought lost, still alive inside dead space and running out of reactor time. Pursued by a Consortium patrol that wants the signal buried, Lior gathers an unlikely crew of castoffs and races to the relay at the edge of dead space to broadcast the colony's location before its reactor detonates. In the end, Lior must choose between destroying their own identity records to save the crew or preserving the truth that could reunite the scattered human worlds—and they choose truth, waking the protocol that reopens contact at last.
about_author: Juniper Ravensworth is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write about the people history forgets. They live on a coastal island with two dogs and an unhealthy collection of decommissioned ship transponders.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A routine supply run to the seed vault establishes Lior's solitary life, their rituals of tending dormant genomes, and the silence of the post-war colonies. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness masking old grief over the family lost in the Silence Wars.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Frequencies
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. While calibrating the vault's ancient receiver array, Lior intercepts a repeating distress call in Old Meridian—the language of their grandmother's generation. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as they realize no living colony should speak it.

chapters.title: What the Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with recorded messages from the vault's previous caretaker, Maren. Deciphering fragments, Lior learns the signal originates from the Meridian Dawn, a generation ship officially declared destroyed. Emotional beat: the pull of inherited duty versus the safety of invisibility.

chapters.title: The Consortium Knock
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A Consortium patrol vessel docks unannounced, 'auditing' the vault. Inspector Vess probes too closely about anomalous transmissions. Lior lies for the first time in years. Emotional beat: fear that survival now requires becoming someone else.

chapters.title: Cargo with Opinions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Lior and Dex Okonkwo, a disgraced engineer hiding aboard Lior's hauler after the audit. Caught stowing away, Dex bargains passage by fixing the failing drive. Emotional beat: prickly first contact; the seed vault gains its first heartbeat besides Lior's.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. Dex helps decode the signal and discovers it isn't just a distress call—it's a countdown, synced to the Meridian Dawn's failing reactor. Emotional beat: reluctant investment; Dex, who abandoned a crew once, feels the past tightening.

chapters.title: Port of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At smuggler station Kettle's Rest, they recruit pilot Sefa Idris and medic-archivist Bram Tulloch, paying with irreplaceable seed stock. Emotional beat: the ache of trading legacy for hope; found family begins assembling.

chapters.title: Vess Closes In
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The inspector traces the signal leak and flags Lior as a person of interest, revealing Consortium orders to let the Meridian Dawn die quietly—it carries evidence of war crimes. Emotional beat: cold institutional logic vs. a flicker of private doubt.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The crew slips Kettle's Rest under fire from a Consortium interdiction net; Sefa threads them through debris fields. Emotional beat: terror transformed into exhilaration; Lior stops being a caretaker and becomes a runner.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In the void beyond charted lanes, systems fail and tempers fray. Bram patches wounds and archives the crew's arguments, seeing in them the shape of a family. Emotional beat: tenderness discovered in dysfunction.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. They reach the derelict relay station Tantalus-9 and find it sabotaged decades ago—deliberately, by Consortium engineers. Emotional beat: betrayal across generations; the silence was engineered.

chapters.title: Voices from the Dawn
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Repairing the relay restores a live channel: the Meridian Dawn answers, and Lior speaks Old Meridian aloud for the first time since childhood. Emotional beat: grief and joy braided together; the extinct language breathes again.

chapters.title: Countdown Mathematics
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Dawn's reactor will breach in six days; the relay can broadcast their position in four—but only if powered by a reactor core they don't have. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into a hard, solvable problem.

chapters.title: What Vess Carries
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Ordered to intercept, Vess instead transmits the full war-crimes dossier to Lior anonymously, then burns their own clearance logs. Emotional beat: an antagonist choosing conscience over career.

chapters.title: The Price of the Core
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The only compatible core belongs to Lior's own hauler—the vault's lifeline. Sacrificing it strands the seed vault forever. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; loyalty to the dead versus duty to the living.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Kindness
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. The crew refuses to let Lior sacrifice alone; each offers their own irreplaceable thing. They settle on a shared plan that risks everyone equally. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing into a covenant.

chapters.title: Tantalus Burns
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Consortium forces arrive; the relay becomes a battlefield. Sefa flies a suicide-pattern feint while Dex installs the core. Emotional beat: courage without guarantees; losses that will not be undone.

chapters.title: Signal Ascendant
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The broadcast goes out—position, language, testimony—as the Meridian Dawn's reactor hits critical. Rescue tugs from three hidden colonies break silence to answer. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by cost; the protocol wakes.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Casualties are counted, including one crew member lost holding the relay. Bram's archive becomes the first shared record of the new accord. Emotional beat: mourning that refuses to become bitterness.

chapters.title: Vess Defects
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Publicly testifying against the Consortium, Vess surrenders to the colonial council and names Lior's crew as witnesses. Emotional beat: redemption accepted imperfectly; accountability begins.

chapters.title: Seeds in New Ground
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Survivors of the Meridian Dawn arrive at the vault, and Lior plants the first genome outside storage in a decade—on soil the colonists bring. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into continuation; the vault becomes a garden.

chapters.title: When the Protocol Wakes
chapters.summary: Full-cast epilogue, Lior's voice framing it. The reopened relay hums with traffic between reunited worlds; the crew chooses to stay together as the route's new couriers. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—truth chosen, family kept, silence ended.
